candidates.offer_name: 48h AI Ops Operating Room Implementation Support
candidates.buyer_pain_hypothesis: Teams have AI workflow ideas but struggle to turn them into safe, governed operating routines.
candidates.buyer_segment: AI consultants/agencies needing governance layer and AI-heavy teams moving from demo to operations.
candidates.urgency_claim: Agentic workflows are moving toward production before governance, observability, and ownership are clear.
candidates.budget_pricing_hypothesis: $500-$2,500 diagnostic range remains a hypothesis until E14 validation feedback exists.
candidates.substitute_comparable_service: AI automation consulting, agent governance advisory, implementation readiness reviews.
candidates.deliverable_48h: Bottleneck map, governance risk map, fastest safe implementation step, and owner-ready next decision.
candidates.trust_gap_mitigation: AI-transparent scope, no production changes, read-only diagnosis, explicit risk boundary.
candidates.owner_burden: Medium: requires owner review of one short diagnostic packet and optional validation script.
candidates.fastest_disconfirming_evidence: Public buyers discuss implementation spend but not AI operating-room or workflow-risk pain.
candidates.strongest_reason_to_reject: Too broad if buyers search for one concrete failure mode rather than an operating-room metaphor.

candidates.buyer_pain_hypothesis: Engineering teams using coding agents worry about unsafe changes, hidden risk, and weak review gates.
candidates.buyer_segment: AI-heavy engineering teams, CTOs, AI platform leads, and consultants supporting coding-agent adoption.
candidates.urgency_claim: Coding agents can create fast productivity gains while introducing code safety, review, and compliance gaps.
candidates.budget_pricing_hypothesis: Comparable spend may come from code review, AI governance, DevSecOps, and audit/advisory budgets.
candidates.substitute_comparable_service: AI code review tools, DevSecOps audits, agent governance consulting, secure SDLC reviews.
candidates.deliverable_48h: Risk inventory, governance gap map, bypass paths, approval workflow, and next validation question.
candidates.trust_gap_mitigation: No repo write access, no secrets, no production access, evidence-only review checklist.
candidates.owner_burden: Low-medium: strongest if packaged as a short owner-operated audit template.
candidates.fastest_disconfirming_evidence: Public evidence shows coding-agent risk but buyers prefer tooling subscriptions over audit services.
candidates.strongest_reason_to_reject: May require more technical credibility and sample artifacts before buyers trust an external audit.

candidates.buyer_pain_hypothesis: Teams have agent workflows that break, drift, or stall in production-like use and need recovery triage.
candidates.buyer_segment: AI-heavy small teams, founders, operators, and agencies with broken or unreliable agent workflows.
candidates.urgency_claim: Production failures compound across multi-step agent workflows and are hard to debug after launch.
candidates.budget_pricing_hypothesis: Comparable spend may come from incident response, workflow automation consulting, and LLMOps advisory.
candidates.substitute_comparable_service: LLMOps observability, AI incident response, automation consultants, agent eval tooling.
candidates.deliverable_48h: Failure pattern map, recovery path, instrumentation checklist, and smallest safe next test.
candidates.trust_gap_mitigation: Work from public docs or owner-provided sanitized workflow; no live credentials or production mutation.
candidates.owner_burden: Low if framed as a recovery map from sanitized workflow notes.
candidates.fastest_disconfirming_evidence: Public pain exists around agent failures but not around paying for a 48h recovery room.
candidates.strongest_reason_to_reject: Incident language may imply emergency support beyond current owner capacity.

candidates.buyer_pain_hypothesis: Buyers know AI workflows are blocked but cannot see which bottleneck, risk, or owner decision matters first.
candidates.buyer_segment: Founder-led AI teams, ops leads, AI consultants, and operators coordinating tool-heavy workflows.
candidates.urgency_claim: AI tool sprawl and unclear ownership slow teams down while creating governance and reliability risk.
candidates.budget_pricing_hypothesis: Comparable spend may sit between founder advisory, operations consulting, and workflow automation audits.
candidates.substitute_comparable_service: Workflow audits, automation consultants, AI ops advisory, governance readiness reviews.
candidates.deliverable_48h: Ranked bottleneck/risk map, kill criteria, fast validation script, and owner burden estimate.
candidates.trust_gap_mitigation: Starts from public/source-provided evidence and produces decision support, not implementation claims.
candidates.owner_burden: Low: light diagnostic deliverable with no production access.
candidates.fastest_disconfirming_evidence: Evidence shows general AI adoption friction but not urgent willingness to pay for mapping.
candidates.strongest_reason_to_reject: Could sound like generic consulting unless anchored to one painful buyer workflow.

candidates.buyer_pain_hypothesis: Teams want to adopt agents but are unsure whether governance, evaluation, and data boundaries are ready.
candidates.buyer_segment: AI-heavy teams preparing agentic workflows, AI consultants, CTOs, and innovation teams.
candidates.urgency_claim: Agentic AI spend may be delayed or wasted if teams cannot prove readiness, ROI, and risk control.
candidates.budget_pricing_hypothesis: Comparable spend may come from readiness assessments, governance advisory, and LLMOps consulting.
candidates.substitute_comparable_service: Agentic AI readiness assessments, governance playbooks, architecture reviews.
candidates.deliverable_48h: Readiness scorecard, top blockers, governance checklist, and next validation/pilot question.
candidates.trust_gap_mitigation: Diagnostic-only; no claims of deployment, no production changes, no customer contact.
candidates.owner_burden: Low-medium: repeatable checklist and brief can be owner-operated.
candidates.fastest_disconfirming_evidence: Buyers prefer implementation vendors over readiness reviews.
candidates.strongest_reason_to_reject: May be viewed as too early-stage or abstract if buyers already demand hands-on implementation.
